batches.objective: Select one Vulkan generated-program optimization from recoverable unchanged-application execution cost.
batches.rationale: The submission campaign retains explicit shader-owner metadata and lower repeated inspection cost without a repeatable UMAP application gain. Driver submission dominates the measured native submission phases. Shared pointer-IR emitter compatibility is freshly validated; compiler correctness maintenance does not reopen a non-Vulkan optimization campaign.
batches.nextAction: Profile Vulkan GPU execution in unchanged UMAP and an inference transfer workload. Retain shader hashes, final instructions, register pressure, scratch traffic and addressing; select a transformation only after locating recoverable application cost. If submission dominates end-to-end cost, retain that finding and choose the next correction from it.
acceptance: Numerical, bounds and alias semantics are preserved through independent physical output oracles; existing runtime and full WGSL suites pass.

Compiler time and allocations, generated-program execution time, full application latency and memory are measured independently against the accepted baseline and pinned Dawn, with declared regression limits and every cohort retained.
batches.stopCondition: Retain or reject one measured Vulkan candidate; no shader optimization or application superiority is inferred from preparation savings alone.
requiredEnvironment: Physical AMD Vulkan provider and final-program profiling
Pinned Dawn control and unchanged application inputs
